grading_method: Evaluator manually compared every requested material part of each answer with the fixed source-backed key and frozen summary; support labels did not determine grades. Key details not requested by question are not mandatory.

grades.question: How are Factory cards, encounter tokens, and the structure bonus set up, and who starts?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle Factory cards; select players+1 face-down and return others unseen to box. Put an encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one face-up structure bonus tile. Lowest numbered Player Mat starts, then clockwise.
grades.observed_answer: Shuffle Factory cards and place a face-down random number equal to players + 1 on the board; return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: “number of players + 1”; “11 marked territories”; “Randomly choose one structure bonus tile”; “The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.”
grades.reason: Factory selection/count/unseen return, 11 encounters, random face-up tile and lowest-mat starter resolved.

grades.question: What starts on the map and each mat, and which mat supplies starting power, combat cards, popularity, coins and objectives?
grades.expected_answer: Character on own home base; one worker on each of two land-adjoined territories. Faction Mat supplies power/combat cards, holds four mechs and six stars. Player Mat supplies popularity/coins/objectives, holds six technology cubes on black-square green boxes, four structures, four recruits and remaining six workers on Produce; action token starts beside it.
grades.observed_answer: The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; the Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and two objective cards. On the map, place the character at home base and two workers, one on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining home. On the mats, place four mechs over Faction Mat abilities, six stars by the faction emblem, six technology cubes in Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square, four structures on matching Player Mat boxes, four recruits on bottom-row circular spaces, and the other six workers on Produce red rectangles. Put the action token beside the Player Mat ready for its first placement; leave one-time Faction Mat recruit spaces empty.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup steps 3–4 list which mat sets each starting value and the starting positions for all pieces.
grades.reason: Map and mat pieces, action-token starting location and correct assignment of starting values resolved.

grades.question: May you skip both actions, repeat a section, use top-row gains below, or take the bottom action first? How are costs and benefits determined?
grades.expected_answer: Must move token to different section, except Rusviet may repeat including Factory. Top then bottom, each optional once; may skip both. May use top gains below. Pay full exposed red-box cost before taking as much or as little exposed green benefit as desired.
grades.observed_answer: You may take either action, both, or neither, but must move the token. Normally it must move to a different section; Rusviet may repeat a section. If taking both, top action comes first, and top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before choosing any amount of exposed green-box benefits; costs and benefits depend on the Player Mat and upgrades. You may decline benefits, but may not pay only part of a cost.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: “may take either, both, or neither, but must move the token”; “bottom first is not allowed”; “pay the full cost” and “as much or as little” of benefits.
grades.reason: Mandatory token move, optional actions/ordering, Rusviet exception, top gains below, exposed full costs/optional gains resolved.

grades.question: Who controls a structure territory occupied by an enemy worker, who can use the structure, and from where may you spend resources for an action elsewhere?
grades.expected_answer: Enemy worker controls territory and resources; structure owner retains abilities except cannot Produce at an uncontrolled Mill; enemy gains no structure ability. Spend resources from any controlled territories for actions anywhere; spent resources go to supply.
grades.observed_answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except the Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. You may pay resource costs using resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
grades.reader_evidence: Control/resources: “An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources”; “You keep those abilities even without control, except the Mill”; resources from “any territories you currently control.”
grades.reason: Enemy worker control, owner-only persistent structure ability/Mill exception and remote resource spending resolved.

grades.question: On a normal unupgraded Move, can one unit move twice, can a transported worker subsequently move, and who can carry what?
grades.expected_answer: Move up to two different units one adjacent territory each, sequentially, or gain $1 instead. All units carry any number of resources; only mechs carry any number of own workers, not characters. Carriage is not the worker movement so worker can subsequently move itself.
grades.observed_answer: No. A normal Move may move up to two different units one adjacent territory each, and the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A transported worker's carriage does not count as its own movement, so it may subsequently move itself; likewise, a worker may move onto a mech and be carried by the mech's later move. All units can carry any number of resources; only mechs can carry any number of your workers, and no unit carries your character.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: “two different units”; “cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice”; carried worker movement and carrying limits.
grades.reason: Distinct-unit movement, transported worker own movement and all resource/mech worker transport restrictions resolved.

grades.question: What happens when a Speed-enabled mech enters enemy workers only, even at zero popularity; may its workers enter that territory by themselves?
grades.expected_answer: Mech stops and cannot move again this turn. Enemy workers immediately retreat home leaving resources; attacker loses one popularity each to minimum zero, still retreats them. Workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.observed_answer: Speed adds a territory of movement to the mech, but entering a territory with only enemy workers stops it and it cannot move again that turn. Those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources; the entrant loses one popularity per worker down to zero, and insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. This is not combat. Your workers cannot independently enter a territory controlled by enemy workers.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: “Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops”; workers retreat; “Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero”; Speed's added step; workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.reason: Enemy-worker-only stop, immediate home retreat/resources, popularity floor and independent worker-entry restriction resolved.

grades.question: When does combat occur after movement, who chooses multiple combat order, and can workers enter or leave enemy-character/mech-controlled territory alone?
grades.expected_answer: Finish all movement, then combats before bottom-row action. Active attacker chooses order. Attacking plastic unit stops on entry and enemy temporarily controls territory. Workers cannot enter or leave such territory independently.
grades.observed_answer: After all units finish the Move action, characters/mechs sharing a territory with opposing characters/mechs fight before a subsequent bottom-row action. The attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: finish moving other units, then resolve combats “before the bottom-row action”; “attacker chooses multiple-combat order”; worker restrictions into or out of enemy character/mech-controlled territory.
grades.reason: Combat after all movement/before bottom, attacker ordering and independent worker enter/leave prohibition resolved.

grades.question: State Bolster and Trade costs and choices; where are traded resources placed and what if all workers are home? What if the combat deck is exhausted?
grades.expected_answer: Bolster $1 for 2 power OR 1 combat card; Trade $1 for any two resources OR 1 popularity. Place resources on controlled territory with worker; cannot trade for resources with all workers home. Empty combat deck reshuffles discards; if both empty draw none.
grades.observed_answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card, before upgrades; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity, before upgrades. Place traded resources on a controlled territory with at least one worker; you cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster and Trade paragraphs give costs, choices, placement/home-worker restriction, and exhausted-deck handling.
grades.reason: Both $1 top-action choices, worker-controlled trade placement/home prohibition and deck exhaustion branches resolved.

grades.question: How is Produce paid and resolved, where do new workers come from, can benefits be declined, and do new workers change the cost already paid?
grades.expected_answer: Pay all exposed red costs before action, must afford full power/popularity/coins. Choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker may produce one terrain token there. Villages produce workers from Player Mat left to right, after payment, so new exposure affects future Produce costs. May decline production/workers. Workers never return to mat.
grades.observed_answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token onto that same territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs apply to future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce steps 1–3 and follow-up: pay before production; new workers left to right; “You may decline”; exposed costs affect “future” actions.
grades.reason: Full exposed pre-payment, terrain production, left-to-right village workers, optional benefits and future-cost timing resolved.

grades.question: What are Upgrade and Deploy costs, placement restrictions and effects, and can a completed bottom action still be paid?
grades.expected_answer: Upgrade oil: cube from any green box to empty bracketed red box, never solid border. Deploy metal: choose mech on Faction Mat, put on controlled worker territory, never lake; uncovered ability applies to character/all mechs, not workers. Costs/coins vary by mat. Completed bottom action may still be paid for coins and applicable recruit bonus.
grades.observed_answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded). Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; place a mech from your Faction Mat on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability then applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures and recruits, you may still pay for a bottom action to receive its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonus.
grades.reader_evidence: Bottom-row actions describe variable costs and placement/effects, then state completed actions may still be paid for coins and recruit bonuses. The rule about an equivalent with all exposed costs is not separately stated.
grades.reason: Gives exposed oil/metal token counts from own Player Mat, placements/effects and completed-action payment. Partial support label/evidence caveat does not leave any requested cost fact unresolved.

grades.question: Where may a structure be built, can it move or be destroyed, and how do Mill and Mine work when their territories are occupied by enemies?
grades.expected_answer: Build costs wood, controlled worker territory, one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Permanent cannot move/destroy. Mill adds bonus Produce territory and produces as worker plus actual workers only while controlled. Mine personal tunnel usable for all unit movement even enemy-controlled, enemy cannot use it.
grades.observed_answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; only one structure total may occupy a territory, including opponents' structures. The Factory is allowed, but lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. A Mill gives a bonus production territory only while controlled; it can produce without an actual worker, and actual workers there also each produce. An uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Your Mine is a personal tunnel for your units even when enemy-controlled; ordinary entry/combat restrictions still apply. Opponents cannot use your buildings' abilities.
grades.reader_evidence: Build rules and structure effects: Mill works only while controlled; Mine is personal movement tunnel “even when enemy-controlled”; opponents cannot use buildings' abilities.
grades.reason: Worker/control structure placement, single-structure/terrain restrictions, permanence and enemy-control Mill/Mine exceptions resolved.

grades.question: When enlisting, where does the token go, what are the one-time bonuses, which action sets ongoing bonus, and how do simultaneous/two-player bonuses resolve?
grades.expected_answer: Pay food; remove any recruit from Player Mat, permanently place on open Faction one-time space for 2 power/coins/popularity/combat cards. Ongoing bonus linked to section uncovered, triggered by self or immediate left/right taking that bottom action, not top/Factory. Announce actions. Active then left then right; sixth star immediately ends. In 2-player opponent triggers once.
grades.observed_answer: For Enlist, take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and place it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat; immediately gain that chosen bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, independent of the one-time choice. Ongoing bonuses trigger when you or either immediate neighbor takes that matching bottom-row action, not for top actions, encounters or similar Factory actions. Resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play the opponent triggers it once, not twice. Ongoing bonuses are Upgrade: one power; Deploy: one coin; Build: one popularity; Enlist: one combat card.
grades.reader_evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits paragraphs specify destination, immediate bonuses, source of ongoing bonus, triggering actions, order, quantities and two-player treatment.
grades.reason: Permanent open Faction placement, four one-time choices, uncovered-section ongoing trigger, active-left-right and two-player exception resolved.

grades.question: What may each combatant secretly spend on dial and cards, how do combat abilities resolve, and how are totals paid and ties broken?
grades.expected_answer: May fight at zero power/popularity. Attacker mech ability first, then defender. Dial 0 to min(current power,7). Up to one card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial. Reveal simultaneously; add card values, attacker wins tie. Both pay dial power and discard used cards face-up; card values do not reduce track.
grades.observed_answer: Combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power from zero to the lesser of seven and their current power. Each may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, including at zero dial power; Rusviet People's Army adds one card if any workers are present. If both have combat mech abilities, attacker resolves theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Each player deducts their dial power from their track and discards every played combat card face-up; card values do not deduct additional track power.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 1–3 specify secret simultaneous dial choice, card limits, ability order, totals, tie rule and payment.
grades.reason: Capped dial/card spending, attacker-first abilities, simultaneous reveal/tie, both dial payments and used-card face-up discard resolved.

grades.question: After combat, what happens to all units/resources, popularity, combat stars, and the losing player combat-card reward?
grades.expected_answer: Winner controls territory/resources, places combat star if below two (Saxony unlimited available stars), may still fight after limit. Loser retreats all units including workers home leaving resources. Winning attacker loses one popularity per opposing worker retreated; winning defender does not. Loser draws one combat card if revealed at least one power on dial OR cards, none for zero total.
grades.observed_answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally at most two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within six available). All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy may instead retreat eligible units and carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, while a winning defender loses none; Polania Camaraderie has the stated combat exception. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed any power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat step 4–5 gives the territory, star, retreat/resource, popularity and losing-card rules.
grades.reason: Winner control/star limit, all-unit retreat/resources, attacker/defender popularity and dial-or-card loser reward resolved.

grades.question: When is an encounter resolved after contested entry, what if the character loses, where do gains go, and do normal action costs/bonuses apply?
grades.expected_answer: Character stops/cannot move again on entering token; finish Move and all combats before bottom action, only if character still there (must win contested entry). If loses token stays. Discard token, draw encounter, choose one affordable option (Polania up to two); pay printed cost and may decline benefits. Resources/structures/mechs/workers go to encounter territory. No additional normal costs/benefits or recruit bonuses; card face-down bottom encounter deck.
grades.observed_answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; discard the token and draw a card before any following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the encounter token stays. Resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no normal action cost applies and no mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses are gained.
grades.reader_evidence: Encounters: after Move and “all combats”; contested loss leaves token; gains go to encounter territory; “no additional normal action costs” or mat benefits.
grades.reason: After-Move/all-combat encounter eligibility, losing-character token persistence, benefit destination and isolated costs/bonuses resolved.

grades.question: Who takes a Factory card, when, may later visitors take one or change theirs, and how do Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions?
grades.expected_answer: Each character first finishing Move at Factory after any combat must choose one available card, return rest; not just first visitor, max one permanent card per player, cannot exchange. Fifth section, optional top then bottom; no corresponding mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses. Bottom Move one unit up to twice (three with character/mech Speed), same stop rules, Mine usable.
grades.observed_answer: Every player's character must choose one available Factory card the first time that player finishes a Move action at the Factory (after winning any combat); return the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card, and later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom, under the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. Its bottom action moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or up to three for a Speed-enabled character/mech; Mine access and normal movement/stop restrictions apply.
grades.reader_evidence: Factory section states each player's first finish, one permanent card, action-section use, no mat benefits, and bottom-action movement distances.
grades.reason: Every character first-visit eligibility, after-Move choice, one permanent card, independent Factory bonuses and Speed/normal movement resolved.

grades.question: When can an objective be revealed, what requirements and discards apply, and what changes for Saxony?
grades.expected_answer: Only own turn before/after complete top or bottom action, all requirements true at reveal; may delay reveal. Place one objective star, discard both objectives to deck bottom. Saxony keeps second and may complete both, unrestricted combat/objective stars within six available.
grades.observed_answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective. You may wait, but must meet all requirements at the moment you reveal it. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony keeps the second card after the first and can score both.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives and agreements paragraph specifies timing, requirements, both cards' destination and Saxony exception.
grades.reason: Own-turn complete-action timing, all requirements at reveal, deck-bottom discards and Saxony keep/score second resolved; specific card text was not requested.

grades.question: Which achievements earn stars, may stars be lost or another player block a goal, and when does the game end?
grades.expected_answer: Six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, eight workers on board, completed objective, up to two combat victories, 18 popularity,16 power. Must place on achievement, each once except combat two/Saxony exception; irreversible and other players may share goals. Sixth star ends immediately, no extra turns/actions.
grades.observed_answer: A star is earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars are permanent after placement even if power or popularity later drops, and another player's star does not block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play with no equalizing turns or further actions.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars and immediate end lists all star goals, their once-only conditions, permanence, nonblocking, and sixth-star timing.
grades.reason: All star achievements, permanence, shared goals and immediate sixth-star termination resolved.

grades.question: If a bottom action earns the sixth star, what is collected first; what happens to pending battles and a neighbor recruit star?
grades.expected_answer: Gain primary benefit, coins and own recruit ongoing benefit before placing bottom-action sixth star. Undo movement into any still-unresolved battle, return units to origin. Neighbor power/popularity star from recruit only after active action, in order active/left/right (clockwise), only if active did not already end game; stop remaining events at sixth star.
grades.observed_answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect its primary benefit, coins and ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, then check active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for the sixth star each time; if an earlier player placed it, later recruit stars/bonuses do not resolve. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to their origin territories; do not resolve another combat.
grades.reader_evidence: Sixth-star sequence specifies collection before placement, active/left/right order and stopping condition, and undoing pending battle movement.
grades.reason: Pre-star bottom benefits, pending-battle rollback and neighbor recruit priority/interruption resolved.

grades.question: At 10 popularity, how much do 5 stars, 4 normal territories plus Factory, and 13 resources add to held coins? Include structure bonus eligibility and all victory tiebreakers.
grades.expected_answer: Tier 7-12 pays $4/star,$3/territory,$2/resource pair. 5 stars=$20; 4+Factory as 3=7 territories=$21; six pairs=$12, total $53 plus held coins and structure tile. Structure bonus even without control. Most coins wins; ties workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, placed stars.
grades.observed_answer: At 10 popularity, each star is worth $4, each controlled territory $3, and each complete pair of controlled resources $2. Five stars = $20; four ordinary territories plus Factory count as seven territories = $21; 13 resources make six pairs = $12, for $53 added to held coins. Also add the selected structure bonus, which is earned even if enemies control your structure territories; the summary does not specify which tile/features are present, so the amount of that bonus is unsupported. Ties after total coins go to most workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
grades.reader_evidence: Final fortune table and example give $20 + $21 + $12 = $53; structure bonus section says it is earned despite enemy control; tie order is listed. The actual structure-bonus amount depends on the selected tile and qualifying features, which the question does not supply.
grades.reason: All requested $53 calculation, structure eligibility and tiebreakers resolved. Exact structure-bonus amount cannot be supplied without a tile/layout; this unasked caveat is appropriate despite partial support label.

grades.expected_answer: Shuffle Factory cards; select players+1 face-down and return others unseen to box. Put an encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one face-up structure bonus tile. Lowest numbered Player Mat starts, then clockwise.
grades.observed_answer: Select number of players + 1 Factory cards at random, place them face-down on the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts; turns proceed clockwise.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: “randomly select number of players + 1” Factory cards; one token on each of the “11 marked territories”; choose one structure bonus tile; “The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.”
grades.reason: Factory selection/count/unseen return, 11 encounters, random face-up tile and lowest-mat starter resolved.

Player Mat supplies popularity/coins/objectives, holds six technology cubes on black-square green boxes, four structures, four recruits and remaining six workers on Produce; action token starts beside it.

grades.reason: Mandatory token move, optional actions/ordering, Rusviet exception, top gains below, exposed full costs/optional gains resolved.

The mech's own workers cannot independently enter territory controlled by enemy characters or mechs, and a worker cannot independently enter territory controlled by enemy workers. grades.question: State Bolster and Trade costs and choices; where are traded resources placed and what if all workers are home? What if the combat deck is exhausted?
grades.expected_answer: Bolster $1 for 2 power OR 1 combat card; Trade $1 for any two resources OR 1 popularity. Place resources on controlled territory with worker; cannot trade for resources with all workers home. Empty combat deck reshuffles discards; if both empty draw none.
grades.observed_answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both deck and discards are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity before upgrades. Traded resources go on a controlled territory containing at least one worker. If all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster: “Pay $1”; Trade: “Pay $1”; resource placement requires a controlled territory with a worker; empty combat deck is replenished from discards, and if both are empty draw none.
grades.reason: Both $1 top-action choices, worker-controlled trade placement/home prohibition and deck exhaustion branches resolved.

grades.question: How is Produce paid and resolved, where do new workers come from, can benefits be declined, and do new workers change the cost already paid?
grades.expected_answer: Pay all exposed red costs before action, must afford full power/popularity/coins. Choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker may produce one terrain token there. Villages produce workers from Player Mat left to right, after payment, so new exposure affects future Produce costs. May decline production/workers. Workers never return to mat.
grades.observed_answer: Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that same territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Revealing new costs by taking workers affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce steps: pay every exposed cost “in full before production”; choose up to two territories; each worker produces; take new workers “left to right”; new costs affect “future Produce actions.”
grades.reason: Full exposed pre-payment, terrain production, left-to-right village workers, optional benefits and future-cost timing resolved.

grades.question: What are Upgrade and Deploy costs, placement restrictions and effects, and can a completed bottom action still be paid?
grades.expected_answer: Upgrade oil: cube from any green box to empty bracketed red box, never solid border. Deploy metal: choose mech on Faction Mat, put on controlled worker territory, never lake; uncovered ability applies to character/all mechs, not workers. Costs/coins vary by mat. Completed bottom action may still be paid for coins and applicable recruit bonus.
grades.observed_answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; move any technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost. Solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; place a mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures and recruits, you may still pay for the bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade — oil and exposed mat cost; Deploy — metal and controlled territory with your worker, never a lake; ability applies to character and every mech. Completed actions may still be paid for coins and recruit bonuses.
grades.reason: Oil/metal resource costs, bracketed cube restrictions, worker/control/lake deployment and ability scope, completed-action payment resolved; no universal numerical cost was requested.

grades.question: Where may a structure be built, can it move or be destroyed, and how do Mill and Mine work when their territories are occupied by enemies?
grades.expected_answer: Build costs wood, controlled worker territory, one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Permanent cannot move/destroy. Mill adds bonus Produce territory and produces as worker plus actual workers only while controlled. Mine personal tunnel usable for all unit movement even enemy-controlled, enemy cannot use it.
grades.observed_answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden, and only one structure total may occupy a territory. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. An enemy unit on the territory does not give it your structure's ability. You retain the ability without control, except a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. A controlled Mill gives an extra Produce territory; it counts as one producing worker, and actual workers there also each produce normally. Your Mine is a personal tunnel usable for your unit movement even while its territory is enemy-controlled, subject to ordinary entry/combat restrictions. Opponents cannot use your building abilities.
grades.reader_evidence: Build: controlled territory with your worker; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden; structures “cannot be moved or destroyed.” Mill works “only while controlled”; Mine is a personal tunnel “even when enemy-controlled.”
grades.reason: Worker/control structure placement, single-structure/terrain restrictions, permanence and enemy-control Mill/Mine exceptions resolved.

grades.question: When enlisting, where does the token go, what are the one-time bonuses, which action sets ongoing bonus, and how do simultaneous/two-player bonuses resolve?
grades.expected_answer: Pay food; remove any recruit from Player Mat, permanently place on open Faction one-time space for 2 power/coins/popularity/combat cards. Ongoing bonus linked to section uncovered, triggered by self or immediate left/right taking that bottom action, not top/Factory. Announce actions. Active then left then right; sixth star immediately ends. In 2-player opponent triggers once.
grades.observed_answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the selected one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed. For the rest of the game, when you, your immediate left neighbor, or immediate right neighbor takes that corresponding bottom action, you may gain its exposed circle bonus. Resolve active player first, then left, then right; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In a two-player game, the opponent triggers the bonus once, not twice.
grades.reader_evidence: Enlist: recruit from “any bottom-row section,” place on any open Faction Mat one-time bonus; ongoing bonus is where removed. Ongoing recruits: active, left, right; two-player opponent triggers once.
grades.reason: Permanent open Faction placement, four one-time choices, uncovered-section ongoing trigger, active-left-right and two-player exception resolved.

grades.question: What may each combatant secretly spend on dial and cards, how do combat abilities resolve, and how are totals paid and ties broken?
grades.expected_answer: May fight at zero power/popularity. Attacker mech ability first, then defender. Dial 0 to min(current power,7). Up to one card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial. Reveal simultaneously; add card values, attacker wins tie. Both pay dial power and discard used cards face-up; card values do not reduce track.
grades.observed_answer: Each combatant secretly and simultaneously chooses dial power from 0 to the smaller of 7 and their current power. They may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial power; Rusviet People's Army adds one additional card total if at least one worker is present. If both combatants have combat mech abilities, attacker resolves theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial power and card values; attacker wins ties. Both winner and loser deduct their dial power from their power track, and every played card is discarded face-up; card values do not cost additional track power.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 1–3: secret simultaneous dials capped at min(7,current power); cards per participating character/mech; attacker abilities first; attacker wins ties; both pay dial power and discard played cards.
grades.reason: Capped dial/card spending, attacker-first abilities, simultaneous reveal/tie, both dial payments and used-card face-up discard resolved.

grades.question: After combat, what happens to all units/resources, popularity, combat stars, and the losing player combat-card reward?
grades.expected_answer: Winner controls territory/resources, places combat star if below two (Saxony unlimited available stars), may still fight after limit. Loser retreats all units including workers home leaving resources. Winning attacker loses one popularity per opposing worker retreated; winning defender does not. Loser draws one combat card if revealed at least one power on dial OR cards, none for zero total.
grades.observed_answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally up to two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within its six available). All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, even workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie waives popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after winning as aggressor, but not when driving off undefended workers without combat. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat step 4: winner controls territory/resources and star; losing units retreat, leaving resources. Step 5: attacker popularity loss, defender none; loser draws a card if they revealed power on dial or through cards.
grades.reason: Winner control/star limit, all-unit retreat/resources, attacker/defender popularity and dial-or-card loser reward resolved.

grades.question: When is an encounter resolved after contested entry, what if the character loses, where do gains go, and do normal action costs/bonuses apply?
grades.expected_answer: Character stops/cannot move again on entering token; finish Move and all combats before bottom action, only if character still there (must win contested entry). If loses token stays. Discard token, draw encounter, choose one affordable option (Polania up to two); pay printed cost and may decline benefits. Resources/structures/mechs/workers go to encounter territory. No additional normal costs/benefits or recruit bonuses; card face-down bottom encounter deck.
grades.observed_answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve an encounter only if the character remains on the token territory; discard the token and draw a card. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. All resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay the encounter's printed cost, but no additional normal action costs and no additional mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses apply.
grades.reader_evidence: Encounters: resolve after the whole Move action and all combats if character remains; on lost contested entry “the token stays”; gains go to “the encounter territory”; no normal action costs or mat/recruit bonuses.
grades.reason: After-Move/all-combat encounter eligibility, losing-character token persistence, benefit destination and isolated costs/bonuses resolved.

grades.question: Who takes a Factory card, when, may later visitors take one or change theirs, and how do Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions?
grades.expected_answer: Each character first finishing Move at Factory after any combat must choose one available card, return rest; not just first visitor, max one permanent card per player, cannot exchange. Fifth section, optional top then bottom; no corresponding mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses. Bottom Move one unit up to twice (three with character/mech Speed), same stop rules, Mine usable.
grades.observed_answer: Each player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if necessary), looks at the available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. This applies to every player, not only the first visitor. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. Use the card as a fifth action section, with optional top then bottom under the usual no-repeat rule, except Rusviet can repeat. Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. The Factory bottom action moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and normal movement and stop restrictions still apply.
grades.reader_evidence: Factory: “Every player's character” chooses on its first finish of a Move action there; at most one permanent card; Factory actions lack mat/recruit bonuses; bottom action moves one unit 2 spaces, or 3 with Speed for character/mech.
grades.reason: Every character first-visit eligibility, after-Move choice, one permanent card, independent Factory bonuses and Speed/normal movement resolved.

grades.question: When can an objective be revealed, what requirements and discards apply, and what changes for Saxony?
grades.expected_answer: Only own turn before/after complete top or bottom action, all requirements true at reveal; may delay reveal. Place one objective star, discard both objectives to deck bottom. Saxony keeps second and may complete both, unrestricted combat/objective stars within six available.
grades.observed_answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective, and you must meet all its requirements at the moment of reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed. Saxony may complete both starting objectives and keeps the second card after the first, so can score both.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives: reveal only on your own turn before/after an action; meet all requirements at reveal; put both cards on deck bottom; Saxony retains the other card and can score both.
grades.reason: Own-turn complete-action timing, all requirements at reveal, deck-bottom discards and Saxony keep/score second resolved; specific card text was not requested.

grades.question: Which achievements earn stars, may stars be lost or another player block a goal, and when does the game end?
grades.expected_answer: Six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, eight workers on board, completed objective, up to two combat victories, 18 popularity,16 power. Must place on achievement, each once except combat two/Saxony exception; irreversible and other players may share goals. Sixth star ends immediately, no extra turns/actions.
grades.observed_answer: A star is earned for six upgrades; four deployed mechs; four built structures; four recruits; all eight workers on the board; one revealed completed objective; a combat victory (up to two stars); 18 popularity; or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars are permanent even if power or popularity later drops, and another player's stars never block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars and immediate end lists all achievements; “A placed star is permanent”; “Other players' stars never block a goal”; sixth star “immediately ends play.”
grades.reason: All star achievements, permanence, shared goals and immediate sixth-star termination resolved.

grades.question: If a bottom action earns the sixth star, what is collected first; what happens to pending battles and a neighbor recruit star?
grades.expected_answer: Gain primary benefit, coins and own recruit ongoing benefit before placing bottom-action sixth star. Undo movement into any still-unresolved battle, return units to origin. Neighbor power/popularity star from recruit only after active action, in order active/left/right (clockwise), only if active did not already end game; stop remaining events at sixth star.
grades.observed_answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins and the active player's ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor, checking for a sixth star at each step; if the earlier player has ended the game, no later recruit star or bonus resolves. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to the territories they came from; do not resolve another combat.
grades.reader_evidence: Sixth-star sequence: bottom action primary benefit, coins and own recruit benefit before star; active then left then right; no later bonus after sixth star; pending battle movement is undone.
grades.reason: Pre-star bottom benefits, pending-battle rollback and neighbor recruit priority/interruption resolved.

grades.question: At 10 popularity, how much do 5 stars, 4 normal territories plus Factory, and 13 resources add to held coins? Include structure bonus eligibility and all victory tiebreakers.
grades.expected_answer: Tier 7-12 pays $4/star,$3/territory,$2/resource pair. 5 stars=$20; 4+Factory as 3=7 territories=$21; six pairs=$12, total $53 plus held coins and structure tile. Structure bonus even without control. Most coins wins; ties workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, placed stars.
grades.observed_answer: At 10 popularity, each star is worth $4, each controlled territory $3, and each complete pair of controlled resources $2. Five stars add $20. Four ordinary territories plus the Factory count as seven territories total (the Factory counts as three), adding $21. Thirteen resources make six pairs, adding $12. These sources add $53 to held coins, before the structure bonus. The selected structure bonus is earned even if enemies control the territories containing your structures; score only the selected tile. Tiebreakers are workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
grades.reader_evidence: Final fortune table at popularity 7–12 gives $4/$3/$2; Factory counts as three territories; example totals “$20 + $21 + $12 = $53”; structure bonus earned even if enemies control your structures' territories; listed tie order.
grades.reason: Tier-2 rates, Factory as three, floor pairs and $53, retained coins/structure eligibility and exact tiebreak order resolved.
